scope: Read-only main-log and crash-buffer classification for the 18-scene cold emulator sweep plus five warm probes. No APK or emulator changes were made by this analysis.
environment: Android 17 API 37 ARM64 emulator, host MoltenVK with Guest ANGLE and exposeES32ForTesting. Emulator-only configuration; physical crDroid results remain untested.
mandatory_interpretation: An empty crashes.txt is not evidence of zero crashes. Unity emits its native crash report to main logcat; inspect E CRASH signal lines and correlate ActivityManager process death/restart.
The original Earth/Mars Unity 2019.3.15f1 allocator fault remains unresolved. The graphics backend improvement does not repair that engine code.

The allocator message mentions virtual-address regions, not proof that the process allocated 16 GB of physical RAM. GPU memory pressure or ASLR may change the trigger; their causal role has not been isolated.
A wallpaper that becomes visible after a process restart has recovered during this bounded sample; it has not passed uninterrupted preview stability.
These results do not validate a physical OnePlus/crDroid build, long-duration performance, battery use, or all warm-service transitions.
Warm Earth/Mars switching also has a separate null-pointer / duplicate-Unity-initialization fault. Neither this lifecycle problem nor the allocator failure is repaired by the emulator graphics flags.
safe_app_side_mitigations: Keep original-port status explicit and offer the corresponding DepthWall native alternative as a user-selected fallback.
Allow the user to retry Android live-wallpaper preview, with the remaining compatibility limitation visible. A retry is not a repair or stability guarantee.
Preserve the current wallpaper when preview is cancelled. Do not force-stop external packages, silently swap the current wallpaper, or reset it to an intermediate wallpaper.
The DepthWall app cannot repair the separately installed port native allocator through its own rendering settings. Do not distribute an unvalidated debug allocator repack as a performance fix.

If an original Earth/Mars package is already active, explain that changing its location may restart or crash the external engine. Do not promise that reopening preview or changing DepthWall quality can fix it.

interpretation: Longji and Bahram each first fault at null address 0x0 on UnityMain during same-package scene switching, then a replacement process hits duplicate NavMeshAgent class registration and SIGTRAP. These differ from the cold allocator signature.

Logs show two Unity initialization threads in the restarted shared package process. Together with static service code constructing separate UnityPlayer instances, this supports a multi-engine lifecycle conflict; it does not prove every later process death has that cause.
Self-directed SIGKILL after lifecycle/timeout events is listed separately from native fatal signals. Other wallpaper packages still running during a capture are excluded from the target scene count.
A warm-window restart count includes the initial process inherited from an earlier scene when its death is present; starts-minus-one would undercount these transitions.
